editorial:
Ever wonder what happens when a quiet, awkward student gets pulled into a glittering world of old money and bad behavior? Saltburn drops you right into that fantasy. You follow Oliver Quick, a scholarship kid at Oxford who feels out of place until he befriends Felix Catton, a charming, wealthy classmate. When Felix invites Oliver to spend the summer at his family's massive estate, the story shifts from campus drama to something darker and stranger. The vibe is lush, seductive, and a little unsettling, like a party you know will end badly but you can't look away from.

The acting is the real draw here, especially the lead performances that make every scene crackle with tension. The pacing starts slow but builds into something wild and unforgettable, with bold choices that will either thrill you or turn you off. The visuals are gorgeous, though the story can feel over the top at times. If you enjoy dark comedies with a sharp edge, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final act, you learn Oliver planned everything from the start. He manipulated Felix's family, caused deaths, and inherited Saltburn. The last scene shows him dancing naked through the empty mansion, now the sole owner, having won the life he always wanted. It is a dark twist revealing the quiet outsider was the villain all along, and the whole story was his long game.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies and twisty thrillers.
